features.title: AI summary reads real commit history from GitHub API, not just post-login webhook events
features.user_visible_behavior: A user who just logged in for the first time picks a repository and gets an AI summary that reflects ALL commits from the last 7 days (and 30 days), including commits made before they logged in. The result no longer depends on the GitHub push webhook having been active during that window.
verification: Use an account/repo whose Event table has no rows for the selected repo (simulates a first-time login), but the repo has real commits in the last 7 days.
Start frontend + server, log in, select that repo.
Verify the summary's commit count is non-zero and matches the repo's actual commits in the last 7 days (cross-check against GitHub's commits view).
Verify the narrative / themes reference those real commit messages.
Verify the commit-activity chart (commitDays) buckets by real commit dates, not webhook-receipt time.
Toggle 30d — count and chart expand to the 30-day window.
Select a repo with no commits in the window — graceful 'no recent activity' summary, no crash.
Repeat with a private repo — still works (OAuth token auth).
features.notes: ROOT CAUSE: server/route/summary.ts builds the summary from prisma.event.findMany({ where: { createdat: { gte: since }, repoId } }). The Event table is only populated by the GitHub 'push' webhook (server/route/event.ts POST /), which (a) only starts recording after the webhook is wired up, so a first-time user has no history, (b) stores Event.createdat = webhook-receipt time, not the real commit timestamp, and (c) stores only payload.commits[0].message (first commit of each push). FIX: source commits for the summary directly from the GitHub REST API — GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits?since={since.toISOString()}&per_page=100 using userRecord.accessToken (already loaded at summary.ts:50-51); follow the Link rel="next" header to paginate. Use commit.commit.author.date for computeCommitDays bucketing and commit.commit.message (first line) for commitMessages; commit count = total fetched. Handle GitHub errors / rate limit by falling back to the existing Event query or an empty result rather than 500. DECISION for v1: GET /commits returns the default branch only — recommend shipping default-branch-only first; multi-branch coverage can be a follow-up. The /event webhook and Event table can stay for other uses but are no longer the summary's commit source ('we don't need that step').
